market.conclusion: This is a falling tech market with fear rising, and a few strong businesses have fallen to good prices because of it. Hunt for long-term bargains slowly, and stay out of short-term trades. Credit and rates are calm, so this looks like a sell-off in tech stocks rather than a wider financial strain.
arguments: Macro: QQQ is below its 50- and 200-day averages, and the VIX is at 24.56 ('elevated'). I give this the most weight. Every stock's swing call starts from this headwind.

Technical: only 17% of stocks are above their 50-day average, and XLK is the weakest sector. Defensive sectors (XLRE, XLU, XLP) are leading. This confirms a broad retreat, not a problem with one stock, so I weigh it heavily.
Fundamental: NVDA, NFLX and ORCL are now at or below fair value on every method. That matters for long-term investors, but it says little about the next few weeks.
Rates and credit: the 10-year yield is at 5.1 and little changed over 4 weeks, and credit spreads are at 3.43 with no stress. This argues against a panic, so I don't treat this as a crisis.
Quant: no signal is validated, and 0 of 556 recorded forecasts have been scored. I give it no weight.
Conditions score: RED, with 0 of 5 checks passing. It is experimental and restricts nothing, so it only backs up what the other analysts already say.
market.change_mind: I would turn more constructive if SPY closed above $720.47 and QQQ above $663.92, with the VIX back under 20. I would turn more defensive if credit spreads started widening. The GDP and PCE inflation releases on 2026-11-25 are the next test.

deep_dive.case_for: It is a grade A business with revenue growth of 83.38% over the last 12 months and a forward P/E of 9.09. At $145.98 it sits below its whole value range of $189.34–$411.04, and its price-to-sales is near the bottom of its own 5-year history. Analysts nudged next-year earnings estimates up 4.34% (unverified Yahoo data).
deep_dive.case_against: The stock is down 31.21% in 20 days, in a clear downtrend, with no support level below the price. Its operating margin of 65% is at the top of its 5-year range, and peaks like that usually fade. Unpaid customer bills grew faster than sales, and insiders sold $946.6M outside pre-set plans. According to the headlines, the company also just reported its first results since its CEO left.
deep_dive.decides: Whether the market accepts the latest results. The first sign would be a daily close above $150.03. Until then, build a long-term position slowly rather than all at once.
